page: Microsoft Azure NC4as_T4_v3 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for entry-level machine learning inference and visualization workloads. It is provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and is powered by an x86_64 AMD processor architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 28.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory allocation of 7.0 GB per core. In addition, the virtual machine includes 189 GB of local SSD temporary storage and supports Premium Storage configurations.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU equipped with 16 GB of video memory. The inclusion of hardware-based graphic and tensor processing makes the instance suitable for offloading compute-intensive vector operations. Networking configurations do not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires explicit assignment of networking resources if external access is necessary.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of a moderate dedicated CPU count, 28.0 GB of RAM, and an NVIDIA T4 GPU provides an efficient resource footprint for workloads that require GPU acceleration without the overhead of enterprise-scale accelerators. The instance is suited for deep learning inference, batch video processing, computer vision tasks, and lightweight graphical rendering.
description: Microsoft Azure NC4as_T4_v3 is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring an AMD x86_64 processor and Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The hardware profile comprises 4 dedicated vCPUs, 28.0 GB of system RAM (7.0 GB per core), and a single NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. It includes 189 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage options, while omitting complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The balanced ratio of dedicated compute cores to system memory, combined with dedicated GPU acceleration, delivers a cost-efficient deployment profile for workloads that do not require massive parallel GPU clusters. It is well suited for machine learning inference, small-scale deep learning model testing, video processing, and graphic rendering pipelines.
